**3B.2 Research Note: Fumio Kishida (2024)**

**Assessment:** Mixed, with some real pro-accountability actions but no strong evidence of broad institutional cleanup. Kishida publicly condemned abuse in principle and took notable responsibility for a historical state-rights violation, but the criminal-justice system still drew credible 2024 criticism for coercive detention, wrongful conviction, and death-penalty practices. I found no direct evidence that Kishida used or tolerated police, military, intelligence, party-enforcer, or vigilante abuse in the 2024 record itself.

- [Video Message by Prime Minister Kishida at the Symposium on Inclusive Society and Human Rights](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/05_message.html)  
  - **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office of Japan  
  - **Date:** February 5, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Kishida said Japan must not tolerate discriminatory treatment or violence against minorities, explicitly tied government policy to the rule of law, fundamental human rights, and human dignity, and called for steady efforts toward an inclusive society.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.2, 3B.1

- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida Regarding the Ruling on a Lawsuit over the Former Eugenics Protection Law and Other Matters](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/03kaiken.html)  
  - **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office of Japan  
  - **Date:** July 3, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Kishida called the former Eugenics Protection Law unconstitutional, expressed sincere remorse and profound apology, and ordered rapid compensation and new guarantees after the state’s liability for forced sterilizations was recognized. This is direct accountability for a past state abuse.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.2, 3B.1

- [Kishida apologizes to victims of forced sterilization](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2024/07/17/japan/society/kishida-eugenics-victims/)  
  - **Publisher:** The Japan Times  
  - **Date:** July 17, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Kishida apologized in person to more than 100 forced-sterilization victims and said the government would move quickly on a compensation framework, reinforcing the impression that he accepted state responsibility rather than denying or minimizing it.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.2, 3B.1

- [World Report 2024: Japan](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/japan)  
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch  
  - **Date:** 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** HRW said Japan’s “hostage justice” system still coerced confessions through repeated arrests, denial of bail, and uncounseled questioning; it also criticized secrecy around death row and the continued use of capital punishment. This is negative evidence that abuse in the prison / justice system persisted.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.2, 3B.1

- [Japan’s Abusive ‘Hostage Justice’ System Persists](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/01/japans-abusive-hostage-justice-system-persists)  
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch  
  - **Date:** October 1, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** HRW said abusive pretrial detention and coerced confessions were still ongoing in Japan and used the Hakamada case to illustrate wrongful conviction and arbitrary punishment. This supports a finding that Kishida did not eliminate abuse in detention and prosecution.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.2, 3B.1

- [Japanese man acquitted of 1966 murders after 45 years on death row](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/japanese-man-acquitted-of-1966-murders-after-45-years-on-death-row-3633320)  
  - **Publisher:** Reuters  
  - **Date:** September 26, 2024  
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported Iwao Hakamada’s acquittal after 45 years on death row, a stark indicator that the justice system still produced extreme wrongful-punishment outcomes during Kishida’s term.  
  - **Question IDs:** 3B.2, 3B.1

**Search gap:** I found no 2024 evidence that Kishida personally ordered, tolerated, or shielded abuse by police, military, intelligence services, militias, or party enforcers. The strongest negative evidence is structural and institutional, centered on Japan’s detention, interrogation, and death-penalty system rather than on a documented campaign of political violence.
